newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures called steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures called steady to higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open steady to higher Friday after trending lower this week on mild weather, ample spot supply and falling cash market prices in the West.
"It's seems to be rangebound. If anything, it wants to break down but it has not been able to," said a West Coast electricity broker.
"We've come down here to pretty good support," a Houston futures trader said.

In over-the-counter trading, September Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $30.00-30.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Thursdsay's settlement at $29.99, and September California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $22.50-23.00 against yesterday's close at $22.73.
During early cash business, firm peak deliveries for Saturday and Monday at PV were quoted at $25.00-27.00 a MWh and those at COB $17.00-18.00.
Technically, September PV seemed stuck in a $29.30-30.25 range and September COB $22.45-23.00 range, analysts said.
On the downside, September PV will likely test chart support at 29.30 and September COB $21.55, they said.
On the upside, September PV will likely test resistance at $31.30-31.75 and September COB $23.30-23.60.
Amid the lack of fresh fundamental news, the power complex would take cue from activity in natural gas futures, market sources said.
NYMEX September Henry Hub natgas futures were up 2.2 cents at $2.450 per million British thermal units in early trading.
Next week, the southern portion of the Southwest were expected to receive above normal temperatures while Colorado and the coastal area were forecast to see seasonal readings.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures would average below normal in the eastern area and above normal along the coast.
Most baseload units in the West were said to be operating normally early Friday.
The 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Palo Verde generating complex in Arizona continued to coast down toward its refueling outage in September.
The unit, in Wintersburg, Ariz., was operating at 83 percent power early Friday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said in its daily plant status report.
